note_text: Sources & notes (Tk crore converted to Tk mn: ×10; blue = hardcoded inputs from reports, black = formulas)

2010: Annual Report (AR) 2010 audited FS. 2011–2016: 'Seven Years Performance of BDBL', AR2016 (restated). 2017: AR2020 5-yr table. 2018–2022: AR2022 5-yr table. 2023: AR2023 5-yr table. 2024: 'At a Glance' table in AR2024 (checked to the audited solo FS).

Total Assets excludes contra items; Deposits include bills payable; Loans & Advances are gross; NII + Non-Interest Income = Total Operating Income (investment + commission/exchange + other operating income).
2012 Equity = Tk 1,569.88 cr (audited solo). AR2012's 3-yr table shows 1,469.88, an apparent typo, not used.
2013–2016 are restated figures from AR2016. Original AR2013 differs (operating income 321.09 cr vs 327.09; EPS 25.50–25.93 vs 22.07; cost-to-income 60.97% vs 50.70%).
2010 Non-Interest Income (103.79 cr) is from AR2010 (ties to total operating income); AR2012 splits it 86.21 + 20.00 = 106.21.
NPL amount = classified loans (excl. staff loans in 5-yr tables); NPL % as reported (2013 rounded as printed). 2016 NPL amount 731.83 cr (AR2020) vs 730.21 cr in AR2016.

Provision Coverage = 'Provision Maintained' ÷ classified loans. 2010–16 from AR2016 table; 2017–22 from AR2020/22; 2023–24 from AR2024 (2024 includes a Bangladesh Bank-approved provision deferral; deficit of 18.46 cr vs required).

Cost-to-Income is now computed consistently as Administrative & Operating Expenditure ÷ Total Operating Income (formula literals in Tk crore). This is the definition AR2024 uses for 2020–2024 (91.50/74.71/71.69/83.09/82.10%).

Previously published ratios used other definitions and are not comparable: 2010–19 reported 55.12/54.92/59.21/50.70/68.61/87.27/89.40/84.97/79.61/86.28%; 2020–23 in AR2022/23: 96.17/98.02/96.97/96.93%.
CAR: Basel II 2010–2012, Basel III from 2013; 2023–24 are solo CRAR. 2011 CAR 28.90% per 3-yr table (AR2012 CAR table shows 29.18%). 2013 NPAT 88.30 cr is restated.
EPS in Tk. Paid-up capital rose from Tk 400 cr to Tk 600 cr in 2021 (stock dividend).
Loan-Deposit Ratio is balance-sheet loans ÷ deposits; very high in 2010–12 (small deposit base) and differs from the bank's reported ADR (168.9%/148.5%/155.1%).
2025–2026: no BDBL annual report for these years has been provided, so the columns are left blank.
Sources & notes (figures in Tk mn; 1 crore = 10 mn; blue = hardcoded inputs from reports, black = formulas)

Bangladesh Krishi Bank (BKB) established 1973 under the Bangladesh Krishi Bank Order 1973 (President’s Order No. 27 of 1973); wholly government-owned specialised agricultural bank, no listed shares (EPS not applicable).

Data sourced from BKB’s own audited Auditors’ Reports & Financial Statements for FY2010-11 through FY2024-25 (14 annual reports); each report also carries the prior year as a comparative column, used to cross-check adjoining years for consistency.

FY2010–FY2013 use the "Statement of Financial Position" / "Statement of Comprehensive Income" format (pre-BFRS terminology) from the FY2011–FY2013 annual reports. These four years do not disclose a Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) as a percentage — only a capital shortfall in Taka (e.g. Tk 6,675.99 crore in FY2013) — so row 24 (CAR) is intentionally left blank for 2010–2013 rather than estimated.

Every year FY2014 onward carries a qualified audit opinion, driven mainly by: capital adequacy far below the Basel-III/BASEL-II requirement (CAR worsens from roughly -37% in FY2015 to -133% in FY2025); non-recognition of deferred tax (BAS 12); short/unreconciled provisioning on other assets and branch/inter-branch adjustment accounts; and (in later years) non-charging of interest on government and international borrowings.
Non-Interest Income = Income from Investment + Commission, Exchange & Brokerage + Other Receipts (excludes Net Interest Income, which is reported separately on row 11).

NPL amount = total classified loans & advances (Sub-Standard + Doubtful + Bad/Loss). Provision Coverage % = provision maintained/held against loans & advances ÷ NPL amount, both as reported in each year’s "Highlights" schedule (FY2010–FY2013) or Note 13.4/7.7 (FY2014 onward).

Cost-to-Income Ratio % = Total Operating Expenditure ÷ Total Operating Income (Net Interest Income + Non-Interest Income, Tk mn); this ratio turns highly negative in years where Net Interest Income is deeply negative and dominates Total Operating Income (FY2019–FY2025), which is a mathematically correct but extreme reflection of the bank’s persistently negative net interest margin — not a data error.

Minor (<1%) figure differences sometimes appear between a year’s own report and the comparative column shown in the following year’s report (different audit firm pairings restated a few prior-year lines, e.g. FY2012 Net Interest Income and FY2013’s Total Deposits highlight). Where this occurs, the year’s own report is used as the primary source in this sheet.

The bank has received repeated government re-capitalisation injections (paid-up capital held at Tk 900 crore; re-capitalisation rising from nil pre-FY2015 to Tk 650 crore by FY2019-20) to partly offset accumulated losses, but capital shortfalls have continued to widen each year through FY2025.

No data available for 1973–2009 or 2026; those year columns are intentionally left blank pending further source documents. Derived-metric formulas (rows 16, 17, 22, 27–29) auto-populate for any year once its inputs are added.
Source & notes
Units: Tk mn. Annual reports state Tk crore for most years; converted x10. Bank-only (solo) statements, not consolidated. Blue = hardcoded input, black = formula.

Sources by year: 1972-1996 AR2013 p.32 (deposits, loans, pre-tax profit); 2008 AR2013 pp.81-82 (rounded); 2009-2013 AR2013 five-year table & ratios (NPL/provision/EPS/2013 statements from AR2014 notes); 2014 AR2014 + AR2016/AR2018 five-year tables.

2015 from AR2016 comparatives (AR2015 not supplied - only the AGM notice); 2016 AR2016; 2017 AR2017; 2018 AR2018; 2019-2020 AR2022 five-year table (AR2019/AR2020 not supplied); 2021 AR2022 comparatives; 2022 AR2022; 2023 AR2023; 2024 AR2024; 2025 AR2025.

Gaps: 1997-2007 not in the supplied files (continuation of the AR2013 'Some indicators' table is missing from the scan). Net profit after tax exists only from 2009; earlier profit is pre-tax (row 32). EPS not available for 2009-2011, 2019-2020. NPL amount/provision not available for 2009-2011 and 2019 (provision also 2020).

Definitions: Loans = gross loans and advances per balance sheet. Non-interest income = investment income + commission, exchange & brokerage + other operating income. Shareholders' equity includes share money deposit. Own-year report used where supplied (e.g. 2023 total assets 793,302 vs 793,508 restated in AR2024).

NPL % (row 19) is a formula: NPL amount / gross loans, so it always ties to the audited note. Bank-printed ratios differ in some years (2012: 26.07%, 2013: 17.48%, 2016: 20.64%, 2017: 23.41%, 2018: 19.21% - different denominator) and 2021 (AR2025 shows 18.84%).

Provision Coverage % (row 21) = Provision Maintained (row 33, loans & advances, general + specific) / NPL amount. Cost-to-Income and CAR are as reported by the bank; where not printed they are computed from the same report's five-year table (see cell comments).
Cost-to-income is above 100% in 2016 (loss year). Net interest income is negative in 2014-2016 and from 2020 onwards (interest paid exceeds interest earned).
The older 'Rupali Bank' tab in this workbook shows figures (e.g. 2025 EPS 4.6, CAR 125%, NPL 5.3%) that do not match the audited annual reports; this tab supersedes it.
